new_entities.name: CRT-D for HFrEF with wide QRS
aliases: cardiac resynchronization defibrillator in wide-QRS systolic heart failure
ICD plus biventricular pacing for HFrEF
new_entities.description: Cardiac resynchronization therapy with defibrillator capability in HFrEF patients with ventricular conduction delay or wide QRS.

edges.effect_quant: Across randomized CRT-D trials, a meta-analysis found lower all-cause mortality (OR 0.55); in RAFT, adding CRT to an ICD reduced death with HR 0.75 in patients with symptomatic HFrEF and wide QRS.
edges.population: adults with HFrEF, wide QRS or electrical dyssynchrony, and an indication for defibrillator-based device therapy
edges.mechanism: Biventricular pacing improves ventricular synchrony, stroke efficiency, and reverse remodeling, while the defibrillator component protects against fatal ventricular arrhythmias.
edges.summary: CRT-D improves survival in properly selected wide-QRS HFrEF populations, not just symptoms. The benefit is strongest in electrically dyssynchronous patients rather than in unselected heart-failure device candidates.
edges.caveats: Device implantation increases short-term procedural adverse events, and the benefit depends on QRS morphology and duration. This edge is therefore intentionally specific to wide-QRS HFrEF rather than to heart failure devices in general.

evidence.citation: Huang XX et al 2010 Int J Cardiol
evidence.notes: All cause mortality of cardiac resynchronization therapy with implantable cardioverter defibrillator: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

effect_quant.comparator: all-cause mortality with CRT-D versus no-CRT-D in pooled randomized trials

evidence.citation: Tang ASL et al 2010 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Cardiac-resynchronization therapy for mild-to-moderate heart failure.
